what_this_is: The HEAD-CHAIN gates (Phase 7): the neck and the head are one rigid chain, oriented by the nose (Nose mode, the default) or by the whole nose+ears face basis (Face mode). Measured on the committed fixture tests/fixtures/client_take — the client's 26-frame take, reconstructed from its 2D by the shipped pipeline — so every number is re-derivable in CI without the client's photographs. This is the evidence for Decision 4, the user's dimensions invariant: detected points may ORIENT the character and may never change its dimensions. The ruling it belongs to is in docs/DECISIONS.md. docs/audit-2026-09/phase5_gates.json is a different question (is the Halpe-26 skull HEAD worth switching on) with its own pre-registered table; the two files share only the take.
recorded_in: docs/DECISIONS.md (the ruling and the deferred re-weight), tools/measure_head_gates.py (HEAD_CHAIN_GATES), tests/test_head_source.py::test_the_head_chain_gates_still_read_the_same_on_the_committed_fixture

before.what: The same four measurements before the chain was made rigid: the neck was aimed at the EAR MIDPOINT while the head bone took the full face basis, so the two bones carried different matrices and the blend between them sheared the skull — 396 head-weighted vertices, only 20 of them above 0.99 head.
before.source: the audit's measurement of this take; the head-aim pair is `fixture_run.head_aim_with_face` in phase5_gates.json, which was written before the fix and still reads 3.7813 / 22.9516.

what_the_gate_is_scored_on: Skull edges the CHAIN owns outright: both ends at least 0.4 head bone and at least 0.999 head+neck together — 678 of the 991 head-weighted edges. That is NARROWER than the rule the gate was first written with, and the narrowing is recorded as `restated_gate` below, with what the wider rule reads here and that it fails: the shear row's own `rule` string says which set it is scored on, so no reader has to infer it. The other 313 edges have an end that also carries CHEST weight (vertex 972 is head 0.43 / neck 0.50 / chest 0.06): that is the throat seam, and it stretches when the chain turns exactly as an elbow's seam stretches when the elbow bends. Decision 4 puts that out of scope in as many words ('not in scope: the normal blend stretch at bending joints (throat, elbows, knees), which is ordinary skinning and was there before the face feature'), so it is measured and reported under `with_the_throat_blend` in each mode — and pinned by the fixture test — but not gated. The plan's in-memory simulation predicted 1.045x for Nose mode on the WIDER set; measured here that set reads 1.0536 (Nose) and 1.1644 (Face), all of it on chest-blended vertices, while the chain's own skull reads 1.0000 in both modes. The same split is why tests/test_retarget.py::test_the_skull_does_not_shear applies the 1.05x bar at a reduced 12+6 deg stimulus and demands exact rigidity of the chain-only edges at 40+20 deg.
why_the_turn_error_reads_zero: In Nose mode the nose is a ROLL reference and `_ROLL_WEIGHT` is 1.0, so `Character._roll` spins the neck until the rig's rest face direction meets the captured nose direction exactly: the residual is 0 to floating point on all 26 frames. The gate's live range is its baseline column — the same angle with the face points withheld, 7.02 deg median and 21.33 deg max — which is what the nose is worth and what this gate would read again if the roll target were dropped, down-weighted or overwritten.

restated_gate.pre_registered_rule: <= 1.05x on every skull edge, in BOTH modes, where a skull edge is a mesh edge with both ends' head-bone weight >= 0.4
restated_gate.rule: <= 1.05x on every skull edge the head+neck chain owns outright, in BOTH modes
restated_gate.reason: On the rule as first written this take FAILS in both modes: 1.0536x in Nose mode and 1.1644x in Face mode over all 991 head-weighted edges, against 1.428x before the fix. Every edge above the bar has an end that also carries CHEST weight (vertex 972 is head 0.43 / neck 0.50 / chest 0.06) — the throat seam, which stretches when the chain turns exactly as an elbow's seam stretches when the elbow bends, and which stretched before the face feature existed. Decision 4 puts that out of scope in as many words ('not in scope: the normal blend stretch at bending joints (throat, elbows, knees), which is ordinary skinning and was there before the face feature'), so the bar is held to the 678 edges the chain owns outright (both ends >= 0.4 head AND >= 0.999 head+neck), which read 1.0000x in both modes. The narrowing is what makes the row true; it is not what makes it pass, and the wider number is recorded per mode under `skull_shear.with_the_throat_blend` and pinned by the fixture test.
restated_gate.cost_if_wrong: On the narrowed set the row cannot fail while the chain is rigid: both bones carry the same matrix, so a chain-owned edge is moved by one rigid transform and its ratio is 1 by construction — the row is implied by `head_neck_relative_rotation` and is a statement of the invariant, not an independent tripwire. The live signal is the throat-blend number beside it, which the fixture test pins at rel=2e-3 in both modes, so a regression that stretches the seam still turns CI red — it just does not read as a gate. And the plan's simulated 1.045x, which was the wider set, is not the number this file carries.
restated_gate.what_would_reopen_it: The throat-blend ratio moving off its recorded 1.0536x (Nose) / 1.1644x (Face), or the deferred re-weight of `character.blend` landing (docs/DECISIONS.md): once the skull is 100 % head bone there is no seam to exclude and the gate goes back to every skull edge. The fixture test asserts the seam still stretches, so that day it says so.
restated_gate.recorded_in: docs/audit-2026-09/phase7_head_chain.json (the head-chain table), docs/DECISIONS.md, and tests/test_head_source.py

gates.gate: skull shear, worst edge over the take (both modes)
gates.rule: <= 1.05x on every skull edge the head+neck chain owns outright, in BOTH modes

gates.gate: head bone vs neck bone, worst frame (both modes)
gates.rule: == the rest offset: skin[head] and skin[neck] the same matrix, every frame, in BOTH modes

gates.gate: head turn error, frames where the nose is used (Nose mode)
gates.rule: <= 2 deg on the frames where the nose is used

gates.gate: head aim error, face points in play (Nose mode)
gates.rule: < 5 deg median with the face points in play
